f4b4bb981e:4ee0b7b156ddef32.title: The Lure of the Aria
f4b4bb981e:4ee0b7b156ddef32.summary: For its fall digital issue, the Loyola Marimount University (LMU) Magazine invited readers to discover opera through a personal, playful guide written by David Davila. The article moves from beloved classics to bold contemporary works, and it dismantles the idea that opera is elitist or out of reach. Opera descends from the communal pleasure of telling stories through music, and it is for everyone. Working under the art direction of Pentagram Austin, I approached the illustrations from the same place: people. Opera is, at its core, a human art form, made of desire, jealousy, grief, humor, and defiance. Rather than depicting grand stages or spectacle, I looked for the intimate moments inside each story, the glance, the gesture, the expression that tells you what a character is feeling before they sing a note. The aim was to make newcomers feel they were being introduced to people they might already know, not to an institution. Client: LMU Magazine Text: David Davila Art Direction: P

f4b4bb981e:140e76cbca592c2f.title: BAROQUE BIOLOGY
f4b4bb981e:140e76cbca592c2f.summary: If you closely observe the genetics of any living being, you'll see everything is much more baroque than functional. Midway between perfecting and contaminating, aesthetics refuse to be domesticated. Biology, like creativity, is immensely messy, caught in the constant cycle of decay, regeneration and return. Baroque Biology is a curated selection of Alex Valentina's works that explores these primordial concepts. Like remnants found on a beach, the elements in all these pieces carry the scent of the sea and subsoil ? rarities like pearls and strange shells that appear precious to the human eye, yet are merely discarded matter to nature. Like an island left to its own flow, here the aesthetics of decomposing natural elements speak of life and regeneration, as if each new idea breathes fresh life into all those that came before it. Biological creativity will endure, no matter what happens.

f4b4bb981e:617b9fc626e16426.title: Written Faces: portraits made of words

f4b4bb981e:04747559c4c0f482.title: SKELTCH Business Stationery
f4b4bb981e:04747559c4c0f482.summary: SKELTCH explores the moment when ideas first appear on paper. The identity is built around a dynamic wordmark that behaves like a piece of typed text, constantly shifting, rearranging and forming new compositions. Its unconventional structure reflects the spontaneous nature of creative thinking, where ideas emerge, overlap and take unexpected directions. This approach became the foundation for the packaging design. A vivid orange palette creates an expressive and instantly recognizable visual presence. The wordmark is enhanced with a dimensional 3D finish, turning typography into a tactile element that extends beyond the printed surface. The result is a visual identity that feels energetic, unconventional and unapologetically bold. SKELTCH transforms everyday stationery into an expression of creativity, where even the simplest blank page holds the potential for something new.

f4b4bb981e:6cdbda89b88fd3e4.title: PARASOMA
f4b4bb981e:6cdbda89b88fd3e4.summary: PARASOMA is a research project we're developing at NastPlas on the body an organism would have if it were formed by two biological systems in a stable association. What interests us is the boundary between them: one region densifies because it has to bear tension, another stretches into a membrane, an interface thickens until it becomes a compartment. We start from documented phenomena (lichenization, extracellular matrix, endosymbiosis, differential growth, structural color) and turn them into organizational rules. What comes out of those rules is speculation, and we keep it carefully separate from what has been established. None of these forms exist, but each one should be explainable. There are 21 open series. Each starts from a hypothesis, carries its own risk and its own palette, and we discard a lot. As the research moved forward, the rules started to feel too limited for a still image. So we developed two applications that are part of the project.

a4977d3fa4:05329293cbb5951b.title: Take a Look at A24 Music’s Custom Audio-Technica Sound Burger
a4977d3fa4:05329293cbb5951b.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:05329293cbb5951b.summary: Summary A24 Music and Audio-Technica launch a limited-edition Sound Burger portable turntable.The Bluetooth-enabled AT-SB727 features a custom red, blue, and green colorway.Priced at $270 USD, the 1,000-unit drop hits A24’s webstore. A24 Music has officially teamed up with Audio-Technica to introduce the Sound Burger A24 Music Edition. Serving as a limited-edition iteration of the AT-SB727 portable turntable, the collaborative release breathes new life into a historic piece of audio tech. Originally introduced to the market in 1982, the Sound Burger is celebrated for its highly unique, compact design that allows vinyl records to spin outside of the main body, enabling users to play physical media without the need for a full stereo setup.Aesthetically, the A24 Music Edition updates the retro turntable with a striking, signature red, blue, and green colorway. The highly portable device features an exclusive panel stamped with an original A24 Music logo design, alongside a special emblem plate to mark the partnership.In terms of technical specs, the internal AT-SB727 mechanism supports both 33-1/3 and 45 RPM records and boasts a USB-C rechargeable battery that delivers approximately 12 hours of playback. Embracing modern connectivity, the device seamlessly streams audio to wireless speakers and headphones via Bluetooth 5.2, while also providing a traditional RCA cable for wired home setups.Priced at $270 USD with only 1,000 units produced, the Sound Burger A24 Music Edition is sold exclusively through A24’s website and only in North America. Pre-orders are now open via the A24 Shop, and units are expected to ship in late January 2027. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:3fa1a55da1794e86.title: 12_Things Rejects The Conventions of Perfumery
a4977d3fa4:3fa1a55da1794e86.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:3fa1a55da1794e86.summary: 'Challenging' isn't a word you'd normally use when describing perfumes and colognes, but its a term that's become somewhat of an inspiration for a new fragrance brand named 12_Things. Founded in London by Charlie Vickery, the brand has been built around a "rejection of conventional perfume language", resulting in notes taken from unexpected sources. Throughout the initial collection of eight fragrances, Vickery explores modern life, particularly one spent in the city. Rather than your typical rose, vanilla, or musk, he opts for a combination of skin, salt, asphalt, oxygen, plastic, metal, ink, dust and air. Even the names themselves are intentionally evocative – some more literal than others: Inkskin; White Dust; Infrastructure; Condensation; Vacuum; Interference; Cold Storage; and Void. "The smells that stay with me are often the ones nobody would put in an advert," Vickery says. "A hospital corridor can hold an entire period of your life. The smell of rain lifting off asphalt can tell you where you belong. I wanted to give those experiences the care normally reserved for more beautiful subjects."Every detail, from the bottle, through to the store itself, is the brainchild of Vickery. "The physical experience matters as much as the image on a screen," he says. Conceptually, Vickery also wants clients to think about the end of the brand – which may seem like a funny idea, considering it's only just launched. This particularly manifests in the physical store itself, which gradually deconstructs as each perfume is bought. Inside the London space, located at 198 Hackney Road, the perfumes are kept inside reclaimed bank vault drawers. "When someone buys a store edition, a drawer leaves with them. Each purchase removes a piece of the room," he adds."The store has an ending built into it. You can see the effect of the transaction on the space, and take part of it home. The brand has the right to end, too. Once it is gone, you cannot repeat the past."Take a look at the…

a4977d3fa4:02cb3c1f2b873fd1.title: Kith and Hasbro Teases the 'Star Wars' Sith Collection With Limited-Edition Figures and Accessories
a4977d3fa4:02cb3c1f2b873fd1.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)

Partnering closely with Hasbro, the New York-based lifestyle brand is bringing the dark side of the Force to life through a meticulous range of limited-edition collectibles, home goods, and premium action figures.Anchoring the release are two exclusive 1:12-scale Hasbro Black Series action figures starring Darth Vader and Darth Maul. Each highly detailed collectible features approximately 20 points of articulation and arrives in custom 1990s-inspired co-branded packaging. The Darth Vader figure includes a lightsaber hilt, a blade attachment, a custom Kith-branded lightsaber effect, and a monogrammed display base. Similarly, the Darth Maul figure comes equipped with six accessories, including two connecting lightsabers to form his signature double-bladed weapon and dual Kith-branded effects.Beyond the action figures, the capsule delivers a range of lifestyle accessories steeped in Sith lore. Fans can grab Canadian maplewood skate decks featuring Darth Vader and Stormtrooper artwork, priced at $85 USD each. The assortment also includes a custom black playing card deck highlighting characters from across the saga, alongside 24x35.5-inch movie posters depicting iconic dark side figures like Emperor Palpatine. Rounding out the collection are heavy-duty natural rubber mouse and media pads showcasing vintage-inspired graphics, epic space battles, and cinematic spacecraft.The Kith x Star Wars Sith Collection releases early at Kith London on November 20. A global release will follow on November 25 at 11 a.m. EST across all Kith…

a4977d3fa4:7a117d434d277591.title: G-SHOCK and HIDDEN.NY Unveil Collaborative Watch
a4977d3fa4:7a117d434d277591.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:7a117d434d277591.summary: Summary G-SHOCK has partnered with the global creative collective HIDDEN.NY for a special-edition timepieceBuilt on the popular GM-2100 series, the watch features a sleek silver finish and signature green accentsThe design pays homage to 1990s street culture while adding a distinctive New York touch to the dial G-SHOCK and global creative collective HIDDEN.NY have officially teamed up to reveal the collaborative GM-2110HDN watch. Drawing heavy inspiration from the street culture and nostalgia of the 1990s and 2000s, the special-edition timepiece seamlessly brings the lifestyle brand's distinctive perspective on art, technology, and design to the forefront of modern watchmaking.Built on the structural foundation of the popular GM-2100 series, the newly unveiled collaborative model arrives with a sleek silver finish. Injecting the creative imprint's distinct visual identity directly into the hardware, the face features HIDDEN.NY's signature green accents placed thoughtfully at the 3, 6, 9, and 12 o'clock indexes. The exclusive offering is further elevated by specially designed packaging that directly reflects HIDDEN.NY's recognizable visual identity.The G-SHOCK x HIDDEN.NY watch is priced at $385 USD. a4977d3fa4:4215b5e5b728f945.title: A Night Out in NYC with Xaviersobased and PUMA
a4977d3fa4:4215b5e5b728f945.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:4215b5e5b728f945.summary: A party for the new Hypebeast Magazine issue with Xaviersobased and his hometown crowd — what better way to spend a Friday the 13th? Last week, we celebrated the launch of The Juice Issue with the cover star in New York City, and between the pop-up signing and live performance, the energy never let up.First stop was Iconic Magazines & Cafe, a perennial Nolita favorite. Fans started wrapping the building hours before Xav pulled up, and by the time he arrived, donning his signature green hair and a new pair of earrings he copped for the occasion, the street was packed. From behind the cafe's counter, he signed copies for a few hours, took photos with fans, and even gave away free copies. Of course, his mom and aunt showed up to show some love.Afterwards, Xavier and the crowd moved the night to lounge one4one just a short walk away. The floor filled quickly as DJs Nurse and Rennessy set the tone before the rapper took the mic for a performance of his own. The setlist included songs from his self-titled album, like "Room service" and "Party at my place," before moving into the earlier "Softer" and unreleased "Wassup W It." Sporting classic PUMA Suedes, that he eventually tossed into the crowd, he kept the momentum up as fans and friends packed in close.This year has been a big one for the under-turned-overground rap star — a debut album, a world tour with Ken Carson, another of his own, all with Coachella 2027 on the horizon — and there's no signs of slowing down. His stage is only growing, but as the night proved, keeping his people close as always part of the plan. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:6356aa44ac5dca9b.title: Ann Demeulemeester and Billy Idol Connect for a Graphic-Heavy Capsule Collection
a4977d3fa4:6356aa44ac5dca9b.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:6356aa44ac5dca9b.summary: Summary Ann Demeulemeester and Billy Idol have teamed up on a limited ten-piece capsule timed to the musician’s Rock & Roll Hall of Fame inductionCreative Director Stefano Gallici draws on Idol’s 1980s image and archive, putting lyrics, song titles and photo references into the graphicsA black leather Perfecto with a burgundy collar leads a lineup of eight jersey styles and a striped open-neck knit Ann Demeulemeester and Billy Idol are celebrating the punk icon’s Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction with a ten-piece capsule collection. The linkup first went public when Idol appeared on the runway at Ann Demeulemeester’s Fall/Winter 2026 show. He then wore a custom look to the induction ceremony itself. This new drop represents the next stage in Idol's partnership with the brand: his musical and visual identity, reworked through the house’s moody, poetic lens. The cuts and styling and graphics of the line follow the look Idol made famous in the 1980s. At its core is jersey. Eight t-shirt styles span standard, relaxed, and micro fits produced in an ivory, ecru and washed black color palette. The graphics come straight from Idol’s archive. Lyrics and song titles such as “Eyes Without a Face” appear across the pieces, along with nods to some of the most recognizable photographs of his career. Completing the collection is a red-and-black stripe on the open-neck knit, and a hero limited-edition Perfecto jacket in black leather with a contrasting burgundy collar. The Ann Demeulemeester x Billy Idol capsule ranges from $350 for the micro t-shirt to $5260 USD for the leather jacket and is now available on the brand's web store, at Ann Demeulemeester boutiques in Milan, Paris and Antwerp, and through select retail partners. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:db278d90582359bf.title: A Look Back at Maison Martell’s Creative Exchange in Chanteloup
a4977d3fa4:db278d90582359bf.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:db278d90582359bf.summary: Maison Martell invited four fashion visionaries to Château de Chanteloup earlier this fall. Serving as the base for a unique creative exchange, the historic estate, which the Cognac Maison has called home for decades, inspired discussions on heritage, craft, and, more importantly, future collaborations.The collective in attendance included Johannesburg-based multidisciplinary artist Rich Mnisi and Nigerian-American designer and image director Ugo Mozie, as well as New York-based designers Brandon Blackwood and Jacques Agbobly. Hailing from different areas of fashion, the experience aimed to bring them together under a shared mission of discovery, where they would find out what shapes their creative worlds.Before delving further into their own practices, the appointed “Swift Ones” explored the journey behind Martell’s cognacs, from the vineyard through to distillation, barrel-making and ageing. The group later took part in a blending experience, where they created their individual blends. The immersion also included the Signature Martell dinner at Château de Chanteloup, providing a gastronomic experience by three-Michelin-starred chef Alexandre Mazzia.The collective then joined heads for a group conversation led by Martell Culture Ambassador Ivie Ani. With the tour bringing heritage into perspective, they spoke about the stories that form their journeys. Reflecting on this, Mozie shared, “Every final expression is built through layers, people, process, material, time, and instinct. That is very similar to how I approach designing and styling; what you eventually see is the result of many different elements coming together with intention.”For Blackwood, an entrepreneur whose contemporary brand is built on visual identity, the experience was more about staying true to what makes you unique. “The brand has been around for generations, but it hasn’t lost what makes it special,” he said. “I think about that a lot as a founder: How to build something with a strong…

a4977d3fa4:dd9b932d0f26688b.title: Noah and Converse Take the Chuck 70 Back to the ’90s in Black Watch Tartan
a4977d3fa4:dd9b932d0f26688b.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:dd9b932d0f26688b.summary: Name: Noah x Converse Chuck 70 TartanColorway: TBCSKU: TBCMSRP: TBCRelease Date: November 19Where to Buy: Converse, NoahConverse and Noah have teamed up on a new Chuck 70 Ox in Black Watch tartan, the navy and green check that began in the Scottish Highlands roughly 300 years ago and later became a mainstay of collegiate style. The pair keeps the focus on its materials and construction, giving the traditional plaid a Chuck 70 built to ’90s specs.The upper does most of the work. It is made from a three-tone woven canvas with the Black Watch plaid running across the whole shoe, so the pattern comes from the weave itself rather than a surface print. That gives the check a richer, more textured look than a printed plaid, and it suits the cold-weather timing of the release.Noah based the shoe’s build on Chucks from the ’90s. The brand removed the wing tongue stitch seen on the current Chuck 70 and swapped in a woven tongue tag, so the profile reads closer to how the shoe looked in that decade. The upper sits on a light brown gum rubber outsole, which warms up the navy and green and adds to the vintage feel.Inside, an OrthoLite sockliner adds cushioning for everyday wear. Noah keeps its branding minimal, placing it on the heel license plate, the tongue tag and the insole and leaving the tartan to carry the design. The release follows the two brands’ Spring 2026 Chuck 70 capsule, which first brought plaid into the partnership.Set your reminders and get ahead of what’s dropping next on Hypebeast Drops. a4977d3fa4:44561a29e25f40bb.title: NORQAIN Debuts the Arctic Blue Independence Skeleton Watch With a Redesigned Bracelet
a4977d3fa4:44561a29e25f40bb.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:44561a29e25f40bb.summary: Summary NORQAIN refreshes its Independence collection with a slimmer, tapered stainless steel bracelet.Narrower lugs and a micro-adjust clasp sharpen fit and integration.The Skeleton 40mm debuts it with a translucent Arctic Blue dial. NORQAIN is refreshing its Independence collection, the sporty line at the heart of the independent Swiss brand’s catalog. The update has two parts: a redesigned stainless steel bracelet for the collection, and a new version of the Independence Skeleton 40mm, which builds on a design that debuted last year.The bracelet, now slimmer and more refined than before, still retains the original's sporty appeal with an asymmetrical design built around NORQAIN’s signature center link. That link has a gently curved lower edge, contrasting sides and a vertical brushed finish, framed by sculpted, brushed H-links with beveled edges.The bracelet tapers toward the clasp for a more balanced fit. NORQAIN has also reworked where the bracelet meets the case, using narrower lugs so the two flow together more like an integrated design. A micro-adjustment system built into the folding clasp lets the wearer fine-tune the fit during the day, and the clasp opens with discreet pinch-pushers on each side so it doesn’t break up the bracelet’s clean lines.The Independence Skeleton 40mm debuts with the new bracelet. Its translucent Arctic Blue dial lets the movement show through, then turns solid toward the edge so the hour and minute track stays easy to read. Inside is NORQAIN’s COSC-certified Calibre N08S automatic movement, with a 41-hour power reserve and a custom NORQAIN rotor visible through the sapphire caseback. The familiar Independence details carry over: hands and indices filled with white X1 Super-LumiNova, and the engraved steel NORQAIN plate on the left side of the case.The new timepiece will retail at £4,220 GBP (approx. $5,544 USD) and will be available through NORQAIN's official webstore and physical stores. a4977d3fa4:a78856cd6ff9752d.title: Lamborghini Proves There Doesn’t Need To Be a Compromise With the Temerario Spyder
a4977d3fa4:a78856cd6ff9752d.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:a78856cd6ff9752d.summary: Summary Lamborghini unveils the Temerario Spyder, featuring its first-ever fully electric retractable hard top.Featuring a 907-horsepower twin-turbo V8 hybrid powertrain catapults the supercar from 0 to 62 mph in 2.8 seconds.An enlarged cabin and 13 driving modes ensure uncompromised comfort and performance. Lamborghini has officially unveiled the Temerario Spyder, marking 50 years of open-top series-production with another bold engineering milestone. A first for any Lamborghini Spyder, the supercar features a fully electric retractable hard top.Rather than relying on traditional hydraulics, the roof utilizes ten electric actuators to tuck vertically behind the seats. This packaging preserves the car’s weight distribution while lowering its center of gravity by three mm when stowed. The entire mechanism operates at near silence, taking 17 seconds to go up or down at speed of up to 31 mph. Underneath, torsional rigidity has been increased by six percent over its predecessor while reducing structural complexity. Power comes from a HPEV setup, mating its flat-plane 4.0 liter twin-turbo V8 with three electric motors. Revving to a screaming 10,000 rpm, the hybrid powertrain churns out a combined 907 horsepower and 590 pound-feet of torque, catapulting the car from 0-to-62 in just 2.8 seconds.Inside, the enlarged cabin gains space over its predecessor, comfortably fitting drivers up to two meters tall, complete with integrated neck warmers and an electronically adjustable rear window that lets occupants listen to the V8 sing. With 13 selectable driving modes, including a three-level Drift mode and quiet all-electric cruising, the Temerario Spyder proves that there doesn’t need to be a compromise when turning a coupe into a convertible. a4977d3fa4:cd571f68ef8be4f5.title: Gucci to Present Cruise 2028 Collection in Shanghai
a4977d3fa4:cd571f68ef8be4f5.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:cd571f68ef8be4f5.summary: Summary Gucci has officially announced its Cruise 2028 runway show will take place in Shanghai on May 17The upcoming presentation marks artistic director Demna's first show in the Chinese metropolisThe event coincides with the 30th anniversary of the brand's original store opening in the region Gucci is officially heading to China to debut its highly anticipated Cruise 2028 collection. Scheduled for May 17, the upcoming runway presentation will take place in Shanghai, marking a major milestone for the Italian luxury house as it celebrates the 30th anniversary of its very first store opening in the country.While the event serves as artistic director Demna’s first show in the city, Gucci is no stranger to the Chinese metropolis. The heritage brand previously hosted runway presentations in Shanghai for its Fall 2012 collection under Frida Giannini and its centenary Aria collection by Alessandro Michele in 2021. The label has also maintained a strong cultural footprint in the region through various high-profile exhibitions, including 2015's "No Longer / Not Yet," the Maurizio Cattelan-curated "The Artist Is Present" in 2018, "Gucci Cosmos" in 2023, and "Gucci Bamboo: Decoding an Icon" in 2025.The Shanghai announcement follows Demna's massive debut Cruise collection for the house, which took over New York City's Times Square last May. Despite wider reports of a luxury slowdown in the region, major fashion houses continue to heavily invest in Chinese activations this season. Notably, Jonathan Anderson will present Dior's Cruise 2028 collection in Shanghai just days prior on May 14, while Zegna plans to showcase its Spring 2028 range in Beijing on June 11. a4977d3fa4:31649fa9e9433a75.title: Maserati Celebrates a Century of their Legendary Trident at AutoClassica 2026
a4977d3fa4:31649fa9e9433a75.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:31649fa9e9433a75.summary: Summary Maserati celebrates 100 years of its Trident emblem at Milano AutoClassica 2026.A rare 1959 3500 GT Convertible Vignale Prototype is displayed alongside the new 490-hp GranCabrio.Historic motorsport icons also headline the showcase from November 19 to 22. Maserati is celebrating a century of its legendary Trident emblem by placing two of its iconic grand tourers side-by-side at Milano Auto Classica 2026. The showcase puts the ultra-rare 1959 Maserati 3500 GT Convertible Vignale Prototype next to the modern Maserati GranCabrio.Built in Modena and unveiled at the 1959 Turin Motor Show, the 3500 GT Convertible Vignale Prototype is one of just six units ever produced. Designed by Carrozzeria Alfredo Vignale under Giovanni Michelotti, the drop-top established the blueprint for Maserati’s modern convertible grand tourers. Having been meticulously restored over the past three years, the silver-bodied classic retains its original 235-hp, 3.5-liter inline-six engine and a striking ivory, red, and gold interior inspired by the Vignale emblem.Placed beside its predecessor, the contemporary Maserati GranCabrio demonstrates the evolution of their design language. Finished in Blu Emozione over a Greige leather and carbon-fiber cabin, the latest iteration features a redesigned front end for improved downforce and a wider track. Under the hood, Maserati’s F1-derived 3.0-liter Twin Turbo V6 delivers 490 hp alongside a new Country driving mode.Beyond the main booth, attendees can explore Maserati’s lineage in the main hall, with motorsport icons 6C34, the Tipo 61, and the 2014 Alfieri concept on display. The Milano AutoClassica runs from November 19 to 22, with tickets available to purchase online. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:5f3569abb159b83a.title: Bottega Veneta Looks Homeward for Spring 2027 With "Colours of Venice"
a4977d3fa4:5f3569abb159b83a.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:5f3569abb159b83a.summary: Summary Bottega Veneta unveils "Colours of Venice," a Spring 2027 photo series shot by Chris Rhodes.Under Creative Director Louise Trotter, the imagery pairs saturated hues with historic Venetian interiors.Accessories spotlight the iconic Cabat tote and the new, 1970s-inspired Verde handbag. Returning to its roots in the Veneto region, Bottega Veneta didn’t settle for just a tourist’s-eye view of the city. For Spring 2027, Creative Director Louise Trotter once again taps British photographer Chris Rhodes to lens “Colours of Venice,” a photo series that focuses on tactile, live-in study of light and surface instead of grand canal panoramas.Rather than treating the city as a static backdrop, Rhodes weaves between intimate interiors and open streets. Pink-plastered walls, intricate terrazzo flooring, rich damask fabrics, and gilded mirrors add textural depth to the clothing. Held close to the surroundings, the garments’ construction and saturated tones are highlighted through the use of natural light, creating a visual dialogue between Venice’s weathered surfaces and Trotter’s contemporary tailoring.Leather goods remain the anchor of the seasonal narrative. Alongside the signature Cabat tote, Spring 2027 introduces the Verde, a new handbag that channels the laid-back ease of 1970s designs into a compact, architectural silhouette. Finished with engraved gold-toned hardware, the Verde features a soft leather flap that lifts to reveal Bottega Veneta’s signature Intrecciato weave tucked underneath.Rooted in Bottega Veneta’s Venetian roots, “Colours of Venice” focuses on an understated conversation between place and craft. By letting the saturated colors and architectural textures take the lead, Trotter and Rhodes deliver a unique perspective on both the collection and the city. a4977d3fa4:4cd8df0728ea3c23.title: Oris and Doraemon Travel Through Time on a Big Crown Pointer Date Watch
a4977d3fa4:4cd8df0728ea3c23.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:4cd8df0728ea3c23.summary: Summary Oris reimagines its Big Crown Pointer Date with Japanese manga icon Doraemon.A light blue dial, red minute track and yellow hands mirror the character.A flying Doraemon caseback engraving marks the 1,000-piece edition. Oris is teaming up with one of Japan’s best-loved characters for its latest limited edition. The Swiss brand has released a Doraemon version of its signature Big Crown Pointer Date, inspired by the original manga by Fujiko F. Fujio, first published in 1970.Conceived around a shared fascination with mechanics and time travel, the timepiece channels the cheerful aesthetic of the 22nd-century robotic cat into a wearable, subtle design. The idea came from Jo Haertel Yamaguchi, Sales Manager of Oris Japan, who drew inspiration from the brand’s earlier Kermit the Frog edition and grew up reading the manga in the 1980s. “I don’t think we’ve ever seen a Doraemon watch as charming as this,” he said in an interview included with the release.The design keeps the references subtle. Housed in a 40mm multi-piece stainless steel case, this special timepiece features a vertically brushed light blue dial that matches Doraemon’s body color, while the red minute track picks up the color of his signature collar. The central seconds hand and the tip of the pointer date hand are yellow, a nod to the HOPTER, the propeller gadget Doraemon pulls from his 4D pocket so he can fly.Flipping the watch over reveals a caseback engraved with Doraemon in flight, a fitting touch given the Big Crown’s aviation roots, along with each watch’s limited-edition number. The fun extends to the packaging. The box sleeve features Doraemon, the back shows his TIME MACHINE, and inside is a microfiber cloth modeled on the TIME KERCHIEF, a gadget that can turn time forward or backward.Priced at 2,250 CHF (approx. $2,667 USD), the Oris Doraemon Limited Edition is limited to 1,000 numbered pieces and is available through the brand's webstore. a4977d3fa4:10163d0c6b326f6c.title: Rihanna's 'Talk That Talk' Achieves Quadruple-Platinum Status on Its 15th Anniversary
a4977d3fa4:10163d0c6b326f6c.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:10163d0c6b326f6c.summary: Summary Rihanna's 2011 studio album Talk That Talk has officially reached quadruple-platinum status according to the RIAAStandout singles from the project including Where Have You Been and You Da One also received new multi-platinum certificationsA$AP Rocky recently teased that the superstar is currently back in the studio working on highly anticipated new music Rihanna continues to prove her immense staying power on the charts as her 2011 album, Talk That Talk, officially reaches quadruple-platinum status. Arriving alongside the project's 15th anniversary, the RIAA database confirms that the superstar's sixth studio effort and several of its standout singles have earned new multi-platinum certifications.Leading the pack of newly certified tracks is the hit single "Where Have You Been," which successfully climbed to 6x Platinum. Additionally, "You Da One" reached 4x Platinum, while the JAY-Z-assisted title track earned double-platinum status. The accolades arrive as Rihanna continues to break records without having released a full studio album since 2016's ANTI. According to reports, she recently became the first female musician to accumulate 200 million RIAA singles units, further widening her lead for the most Diamond singles by any woman. ANTI itself remains a dominant force, tallying over 508 weeks on the Billboard 200—a historical benchmark among Black female artists.Despite early reports indicating that her next album would feature a reggae sound, Rihanna previously revealed she scrapped those plans to avoid genre limitations and protect the standard of her work. Noting that she refuses to put out anything mediocre after an eight-year wait, she emphasized that the music "has to matter." However, during an August appearance on The Jason Lee Show, A$AP Rocky slipped up and teased fans with a promising update, stating that Rihanna is "in the studio right now" and "cooking." a4977d3fa4:ecb09028b3e74cb6.title: Christie's Introduces Pop Culture Category in Asia With Rare Pokémon Card Auction
a4977d3fa4:ecb09028b3e74cb6.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:ecb09028b3e74cb6.summary: Summary Christie's is officially introducing Pop Culture as a new collecting category in Asia through an upcoming online art saleThe curated selection features a variety of highly graded PSA 10 Pokémon cards carefully chosen for their extreme rarity and pristine conditionThe eight exclusive lots are currently on public view at the Henderson before the auction officially goes live later this month Christie's is officially introducing Pop Culture as a new collecting category in Asia with a highly anticipated auction featuring rare Pokémon trading cards. Serving as part of the institution's upcoming 20th/21st Century Art Online Sale, the event marks the very first time that the beloved trading cards have been offered within a global sale for the prestigious auction house.The curated offering underscores a growing shift in the collectibles market, highlighting how Millennial and Gen Z collectors are driving demand for categories that seamlessly blend cultural significance with deep nostalgia. Emphasizing premium quality and strict authenticity, the auction house has assembled an exceptional group of cards that represent the highest standards within the space, with the featured pieces carrying a flawless PSA 10 grade.Highlighting the auction's artistic crossover appeal, the selection includes some of the most iconic cards inspired by celebrated fine art. Standout lots feature the coveted Pokémon × Munch series—including Mimikyu, Psyduck, and Pikachu—alongside the highly sought-after Pikachu with Grey Felt Hat from the official Pokémon × Van Gogh Museum collaboration. The timing of the exclusive offering is particularly momentous, as it arrives during the year of the Pokémon franchise's 30th anniversary.The Christie's 20th/21st Century Art Online Sale featuring the eight Pokémon card lots runs until November 27 via the auction house's official platform, with the pieces currently on public at the Christie's Asia headquarters. a4977d3fa4:2ab434fa60a9510b.title: Aston Martin Trades Tarmac for Sand With ‘Call of Duty’ Off-Roader
a4977d3fa4:2ab434fa60a9510b.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:2ab434fa60a9510b.summary: Summary Aston Martin will debut the Dreadnought at the 2027 Dakar Rally.The Dreadnought is a vehicle adapted from the video game 'Call of Duty'.The all-star driver lineup includes champions Alonso, Loeb, and Moraes. Aston Martin is officially trading the pristine tarmac of Formula 1 for the unforgiving dunes of the Sahara. Aston Martin Racing will be making its debut at the 2027 Dakar Rally. Partnering with motorsport powerhouse Prodrive, Aston Martin is preparing to enter three Dreadnought competition vehicles, driven by a star-studded roster.The vehicle they’re entering is one of the most unique in the brand’s century-long history: the Aston Martin Dreadnought. Originally conceived for the video game Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, the Dreadnought has been transformed from pixels into a purpose-built rally raider. Engineered to master grueling distances, brutal terrain, and extreme heat, the Dreadnought represents a significant contrast, both aesthetically and mechanically, from Aston Martin’s traditional sleek grand tourers.To tame these bespoke machines, Aston Martin has assembled a star-studded roster. Leading the lineup is two-time Formula 1 World Champion Fernando Alonso, who will take on the Dakar rally in addition to the F1 calendar. Alonso, who previously competed in the 2020 Dakar, will be reunited with five-time Dakar motorcycle champion Marc Coma as his co-driver. Joining him in the second Dreadnought is nine-time World Rally Championship icon Sébastien Loeb alongside co-driver Fabian Lurquin, hoping to finally secure a long-sought victory. Rounding out the trio is reigning FIA World Rally Raid Champion Lucas Moraes, who will be joined by co-driver Pablo Moreno.The 2027 Dakar Rally is going to be a grueling 15-day test of human and mechanical limits. The 12-stage event officially starts on January 10 from the 30,000-seat Algarve stadium in Portugal with a 300-kilometer opening stage. a4977d3fa4:7874010f2a9f19c7.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:7874010f2a9f19c7.summary: Summary H. Moser & Cie. drops the 100-piece Pioneer Tourbillon Arctic Fizz in 40mm titanium.Features a frosted Arctic Blue fumé dial, rotating bezel, and 120-meter water resistance.Powered by the automatic double-hairspring HMC 805 calibre, priced around $65,950 USD. H. Moser & Cie. is taking the tourbillon out of the boardroom and into the water. Joining a 20-man field that now includes recent additions Gary Woodland and Rickie Fowler, Woods will take on the strenuous 72-hole event from December 3 to December 6, where players are strictly prohibited from using golf carts.The impending December tee time marks Woods' first PGA Tour appearance since missing the cut at the 2024 Open Championship at Scotland's Royal Troon Golf Club. This was followed by a seventh back surgery in October 2025 to replace a disk in his lower back. More recently, Woods announced a temporary step away from the game in late March to seek treatment and focus on his health at an in-patient facility in Switzerland following a reckless driving plea deal in Martin County, Florida. a4977d3fa4:5521296f79683cf4.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:5521296f79683cf4.summary: Most people recognize Vibram by the signature yellow octagon on the bottom of their favorite boots, though far fewer have seen where those outsoles actually come from. From November 4 to 6, the brand opened the doors of its US headquarters in North Brookfield, Massachusetts, for the second edition of Made in North Brookfield. This year’s program brought together 15 creators, designers and brand partners from across the US and Canada, including Nicole McLaughlin, Ella Emhoff, Bailey Goldberg, John Chen of ArchivePDF, Gabriele Fazi of Kith and Victoria Wells of Arc’teryx. The three days centered on New England craft and American bootmaking heritage.North Brookfield is Vibram’s primary US manufacturing center, with factory roots in Massachusetts dating back to 1965. Now owned by Vibram, the plant makes soles for everything from industrial footwear to a classic American boot. It is one of the only rubber outsole factories operating in the US.The experience kicked off with a tour led by Christopher Nikopoulos, Vibram’s US VP of Operations, following the process from start to finish. In compounding, raw rubber is blended with custom performance formulas and colors. Milling then rolls the rubber into precise sheets, known as “breads,” ready for molding. Finally, in the molding presses, heat and high pressure vulcanize the sheets into finished outsoles with their final shape and tread.From there, the creators took over. In the boot and sole workshop, each one chose a custom rubber colorway and tread. They worked with either rubber pellets or shapes cut from rubber sheets, and placed the rubber into the molds themselves. The signature moment came with the yellow octagon: a separate piece of yellow rubber, made from its own special compound, set into the mold as the brand’s mark of quality.With the soles complete, focus shifted to the uppers. Supported by Easymoc, one of Maine’s last traditional bootmakers, the workshop used handcrafted Old Port uppers from the brand’s…

"NO SEASONS is all about material. And so is our work," NM3 co-founder Nicolò Ornaghi told Hypebeast. "We solve all the design problem[s] basically using one single detail. a4977d3fa4:98598c32fd376e57.summary: Summary Nike debuts Tuned Air, a digital printing process for custom cushioning.It removes rigid structures to create tailored, limitless underfoot sensations.The technology launches for runners in late 2027 before broader expansion. Nike has introduced Tuned Air, a new way of making its Air cushioning units that the brand presents as the next chapter in nearly 50 years of Air innovation.Instead of relying on traditional pins, rigid zones and the unit’s height to shape how Air behaves, Tuned Air uses a proprietary digital ink printed inside each unit, which Nike says took about a decade to develop. A selective lamination process then bonds the unit’s internal core only where no ink has been applied, letting Nike’s engineers control each unit’s internal structure with much greater precision.The result opens up a far wider range of shapes, geometries and visual designs, giving Nike finer control over how Air looks, feels and performs. The name has precedent: “Tuned Air” was also the cushioning system behind the Air Max Plus, the 1998 runner better known as the TN, though Nike’s announcement presents the new technology on its own terms.Following an exclusive sneak peek during Nike's World of Athletes showcase in this month, the innovative cushioning system is scheduled to make its official retail debut for runners in late 2027. This initial performance running launch will serve as the foundation for a much wider expansion, with the Tuned Air technology slated to be integrated across multiple athletic disciplines and the broader Nike Sportswear lineup. By removing long-standing mechanical manufacturing constraints, Nike aims to scale this tailored underfoot experience rapidly, marking the beginning of a highly adaptable new era for its nearly 50-year-old Air legacy.Set your reminders and get ahead of what’s dropping next on Hypebeast Drops. a4977d3fa4:9ab347a80b7d0b02.title: The Slim d’Hermès “Sous le charme d’Orphée” Brings the Myth of Orpheus to the Wrist
a4977d3fa4:9ab347a80b7d0b02.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:9ab347a80b7d0b02.summary: Summary Hermès adapts Alice Shirley’s Sous le charme d’Orphée scarf into a Slim d’Hermès dial.Engraving, miniature painting and pink opal cabochons depict a horse beneath a pomegranate tree.Only 12 white gold pieces will be made. Hermès has unveiled an artistic addition to its minimalist dress watch family with the Slim d'Hermès Sous le charme d'Orphée limited edition. Drawing direct inspiration from the silk scarf of the same name designed by British artist Alice Shirley, the timepiece translates mythological storytelling onto a miniature nocturnal canvas.Framed within the collection's signature slender 39.5mm white gold case, the dial depicts a horse galloping beneath a pomegranate tree under a shower of stars, which is a poetic nod to Orpheus, the legendary master of the lyre whose music enchanted the gods of the Underworld.Bringing this fanciful scene to life requires an intricate convergence of traditional métiers d'art techniques executed across multiple stages. Set against a deep midnight blue enamel background, an engraver first sculpts the pomegranate tree across multiple levels to reveal the organic grain of the trunk and the delicate taper of its branches.Several crafts come together on the dial. An engraver first carves the tree in layers, bringing out the grain of the trunk and the detail of each branch. A miniature painter then adds color one layer at a time, building up the leaves, the horse, the butterflies and the flowers. Finally, pink opal cabochons are set individually as the pomegranate fruits, adding depth and a soft shine to the scene. The finished dial is engraved, enameled, painted and gem-set, and the “Hermès-Paris” signature is painted in gold at its base.Inside, beats the in-house Manufacture Hermès H1950, an ultra-thin self-winding movement just 2.6mm thick, running at 21,600 vph with a 48-hour power reserve and showing hours and minutes only. A smooth alligator strap in “bleu abysse,” made using traditional Hermès leather skills, is…

a4977d3fa4:b1d954c9dfb3cc07.title: Fritz Hansen and ssstein Merge Fashion and Furniture in New Collaborative Capsule
a4977d3fa4:b1d954c9dfb3cc07.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:b1d954c9dfb3cc07.summary: Summary Fritz Hansen and ssstein unite for a limited furniture and apparel collection.The capsule reimagines Arne Jacobsen's iconic Series 7™ chair and Dot™ stool.Available exclusively at Isetan Shinjuku from November 25 to December 20. Danish furniture house Fritz Hansen and Japanese label ssstein have teamed up on a limited collection that brings furniture and fashion together. Rooted in a shared pursuit of timeless design, the collaboration explores the intersection where fashion meets furniture. By bringing two distinct design philosophies together, the joint effort opens up exciting new possibilities for contemporary design.The furniture segment of the collaboration centers around two unmistakable Arne Jacobsen icons: the Series 7™ chair and the Dot™ stool. ssstein gracefully reinterprets both of these classic silhouettes through its distinctive approach to materials and a highly refined sense of color. The underlying concept of the release offers a new perspective on homeware, emphasizing that each piece gradually develops its own unique character over time and is only considered truly complete after years of everyday use.Complementing the reimagined furniture, the Fritz Hansen x ssstein collaboration also features a curated apparel line consisting of a cow nubuck short zip jacket, a loopwheel cotton sweatshirt, and a tote bag. The limited collection will be available exclusively at the "AS IT IS, ANEW" pop-up located in the Isetan Shinjuku Main Building (5F), running strictly from November 25 to December 20, 2026. a4977d3fa4:2d6d127dc6014dea.title: Inside Denis Villeneuve’s Decision to Cast Robert Pattinson as James Bond
a4977d3fa4:2d6d127dc6014dea.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:2d6d127dc6014dea.summary: Summary Denis Villeneuve confirmed to ‘GQ’ that he chose Robert Pattinson as James Bond, in consultation with his producers and the studioHis list for the role starts with a believable killer and runs through charisma, sensuality, dark humor and physical strengthCasting took longer than fans expected because Villeneuve made the franchise wait until he wrapped ‘Dune: Part Three’ Denis Villeneuve has broken down exactly what he wanted when he cast Robert Pattinson as James Bond for the franchise’s 26th film. In his GQ Men of the Year interview, the director went through the role trait by trait, describing a 007 built less around gadgets and tailoring and more around menace, magnetism and nerve.Villeneuve’s first requirement is that the audience has to buy Bond as someone capable of killing. “The first quality is that I need to believe that this man is a killer, because more than a spy, Bond is an assassin,” he told GQ. He also wants a visible rage behind the eyes, a quality he says only some actors have.Presence comes next on his list, starting with a kind of panache that doesn’t apologize for itself. Villeneuve described a man who pulls the whole room toward him the moment he walks in, with charisma strong enough to carry a scene on its own. He also wants Bond to be openly sensual, someone people are drawn to and who visibly enjoys himself.The rougher traits matter just as much to him. Villeneuve wants a Bond with a dark sense of humor, who seems to enjoy being in serious trouble and doesn’t mind getting his hands dirty. Physically, he called for someone strong and muscular, a real force on screen. He finished with intelligence, describing a Bond whose eyes show he’s always a step ahead of the audience.The final decision was Villeneuve’s, made together with his producers and the studio, and he knows it won’t please everyone. “At the end of the day, the truth is, no matter who I choose, some people will be excited and others will be disappointed,” he said. The footage picks up with the San-Ti still headed for Earth and turns its focus to how people are living with a threat they can’t stop.The new season moves on from the shock of first contact into a slower kind of dread, where the arrival is certain and the only question is how humanity responds. “We know there is a hostile alien civilization out there, the San-Ti, and they’re coming our way,” co-creator David Benioff said on Netflix Tudum. Co-creator Alexander Woo frames the season around whether the public has grown numb to the danger, and whether some people have started to welcome it.That split runs through Tatiana Haas, played by Marlo Kelly, a true believer in the San-Ti who will go to extreme lengths to advance their agenda. Benioff explains that part of the aliens’ human support comes from people who believe humanity has failed to take care of the planet, which makes the coming invasion feel like a verdict to some of them.Most of the Season 1 ensemble returns. a4977d3fa4:d8543d9df57376cc.summary: Summary British grime artist Skepta collaborated with Land Rover Classic Works to create a bespoke Defender Classic pick-up truckThe one-off commission took 18 months to build and is based on a 110-inch wheelbase variantThe custom 4x4 features a metallic Bronze exterior, Pillar Box Red leather and a 405-horsepower V-8 engine British grime artist and MAINS fashion label founder Skepta brought his distinct vision to the automotive world, collaborating with Land Rover Classic Works to create a custom Defender Classic pick-up truck. Refusing to wait for a rumored current-generation Defender truck, the artist bypassed the anticipation by commissioning this bespoke, one-off build. The project took 18 months to complete, allowing Skepta to seamlessly integrate his personal world and the MAINS brand into the classic 4x4 identity. The finished vehicle merges contemporary fashion branding with classic off-road heritage.The architecture of this exclusive machine utilizes the previous-generation boxy Defender, specifically based on the extended 110-inch wheelbase variant. The custom exterior transforms the traditional silhouette with a cab that ends at the B-pillar and carries a metallic Bronze paint finish. Exterior equipment outfits the truck with a roof rack, a rugged roll cage and roof-mounted LED spotlights. The vehicle rides on aggressive 18-inch Sawtooth wheels wrapped in chunky all-terrain tires and features MAINS exterior badging. Out back, the custom truck bed provides enough space for traditional cargo or an impromptu DJ booth.Inside the five-seat cabin, utilitarian roots give way to high-end curation. The front row includes two Recaro sport models, while the entire interior is richly upholstered in Pillar Box Red leather with sleek Ebony trim. This specific red interior color drew direct inspiration from the shade of Skepta's children's shoes. d006da4fe3:eea75378d009c570.title: America’s AI Ambitions Depend on Taiwan
d006da4fe3:eea75378d009c570.author: Lin Chia-lung
d006da4fe3:eea75378d009c570.summary: The United States and China are locked in a global competition to determine who will dominate artificial intelligence and whether it will be democracies or autocracies that set the standards and values of the new digital age. The United States leads the world in the sophistication and power of its artificial intelligence models, and its innovation base and investment in research and development remain unparalleled.But AI competition is much broader than modeling alone. It encompasses a technology ecosystem that includes power generation, servers, and deployment in real-world applications. Jensen Huang, co-founder and CEO of Nvidia, has described the AI industry as a five-layer cake with energy at its base and chips, infrastructure, models, and applications above it. To win the AI race with China, the United States needs to maintain or establish an advantage in each of these layers. And to do that, the United States needs Taiwan.

d006da4fe3:7c8255a6f6b6499e.title: The New Energy Stalemate in Ukraine
d006da4fe3:7c8255a6f6b6499e.author: Tatiana Mitrova, Sergey Vakulenko
d006da4fe3:7c8255a6f6b6499e.summary: Tatiana Mitrova, a fellow at Columbia University’s Center on Global Energy Policy and former energy scholar at Moscow’s Russian Academy of Sciences, and Sergey Vakulenko, an oil and gas expert at Carnegie’s Russia Eurasia Center, argue that Russia and Ukraine are locked in an energy war that has become an adaptation spiral, despite growing human and economic costs and despite current US pressure on Ukraine. They observe Ukraine’s remarkable ability to withstand Russian strikes, while questioning claims that long-range Ukrainian strikes will be able to achieve game-changing damage on Russia. Ukraine and Russia have transformed the role of energy warfare in modern conflict, drawing on low costs drones but also new forms of technological resilience that are likely to make wars longer and more dangerous.

d006da4fe3:5ad44315d0de90d6.summary: Monica de Bolle, an expert in Brazilian economic policy, makes an authoritative argument that Brazil’s economic problems will persist no matter the outcome of the country’s presidential election. A Flávio Bolsonaro administration would fare no better than Lula when it comes to reducing debt and delivering growth—and Bolsonaro’s illiberal policies could make the economic picture even worse.

d006da4fe3:d2da9274feed5e6c.title: A Less-Is-More Strategy for America
d006da4fe3:d2da9274feed5e6c.author: Barry R. Posen
d006da4fe3:d2da9274feed5e6c.summary: Barry Posen, a professor at MIT, is one of America's leading experts on international security. He argues that the United States military is breaking down because it has been overused and overextended over the last 30 years, and that the only way to repair it is for Washington to exercise much more restraint.

d006da4fe3:e407454ddc8200e6.title: How Russia Sees the World Now

d006da4fe3:e407454ddc8200e6.summary: Dmitry Adamsky, an expert on Russian security and Russian nuclear deterrence strategy at Harvard and Reichman Universities, examines a large-scale shift in Russia’s strategic thinking over the past year, centered around the view that Europe, rather than the United States, is now Russia’s primary geopolitical rival and adversary, and looking at the consequences of this shift for US efforts to end the war in Ukraine.

d006da4fe3:f2fe497a723c80df.title: AI Is a Choice
d006da4fe3:f2fe497a723c80df.author: Alex Imas, Mohamed A. El-Erian, James Manyika
d006da4fe3:f2fe497a723c80df.summary: Alex Imas, Mohamed El-Erian, and James Manyika, leading voices at the intersection of business and technology, argue that realizing AI’s potential requires giving workers, communities, AI labs, infrastructure developers, and big companies a share of the gains. Using insights from game theory, they argue that increased cooperation can make AI work for all.

d006da4fe3:26bb42beb62831bc.title: The China Price
d006da4fe3:26bb42beb62831bc.author: Zongyuan Zoe Liu
d006da4fe3:26bb42beb62831bc.summary: In 1971, as the international monetary system was on the brink of collapse, U.S. Treasury Secretary John Connally told a group of worried European finance ministers that the dollar was “our currency, but your problem.” The dollar had become that system’s official reserve currency in 1944, under the Bretton Woods agreement, making signatories subject to the whims of U.S. monetary policy. Even after Bretton Woods collapsed and many currencies floated freely, the dollar continued to dominate. In the last half century, U.S. currency power has only expanded, as more countries have integrated into the global economy and therefore grown to depend on the dollar. China, reliant on export-driven growth, is foremost among them.

d006da4fe3:8d3c26580c9ed628.title: Empires of AI
d006da4fe3:8d3c26580c9ed628.author: Niall Ferguson, Lisa Klaassen, Eric Schmidt
d006da4fe3:8d3c26580c9ed628.summary: In this essay, Niall Ferguson, one of the world’s foremost experts on imperial history, teams up the former CEO of Google, Eric Schmidt, and the researcher Lisa Klaasen to make the provocative argument that AI is an inherently “imperial technology”—and to reveal what the fate of past empires might say about the future of U.S.-Chinese competition in a world shaped by AI.

d006da4fe3:5932b197c4f8ad1c.summary: William McRaven, a retired four-star admiral and a major figure in American military affairs, uses history and his personal experiences to make an authoritative case that American leaders frequently overestimate the potential of military force to achieve political ends—and that new technologies like AI will exacerbate this problem.

d006da4fe3:33fc15a61a4dba01.title: “Earth Satellites and Foreign Policy”
d006da4fe3:33fc15a61a4dba01.summary: The advent of a new technology invariably comes with strategic implications, raising the question of who will benefit and whether risks can be managed. In 1957, following the Soviet Sputnik launch, U.S. policymakers and analysts recognized that the satellite, as the American physicist and engineer Lloyd Berkner observed in these pages, would bring transformative effects. The United States could not risk losing out, Berkner argued, but nor should governments allow geopolitical tensions to prevent the technology’s broad benefits from emerging.

d006da4fe3:9729d1ab8b25d3aa.title: Europe’s Credibility Gap
d006da4fe3:9729d1ab8b25d3aa.author: Claas Mertens, Ngaire Woods
d006da4fe3:9729d1ab8b25d3aa.summary: Ngaire Woods, Dean of Oxford’s Blavatnik School of Government, Claas Mertens, also at Oxford, have written a piece arguing that Europe, despite its attempts at self-sufficiency, remains dependent on an unpredictable United States. The continent needs to address this vulnerability so that it can convince other countries, many of which find themselves similarly vulnerable to great-power coercion, that it is a worthy partner.

d006da4fe3:09191e7fdf89ba60.title: A Better “America First”

d006da4fe3:09191e7fdf89ba60.summary: Charles Kupchan, who served in the Clinton and Obama administrations, argues that many aspects of Trump's foreign policy are worth keeping and align with changes in the international system. He explains how the next president can marry the good impulses of "America first" with the best of liberal internationalism.

d006da4fe3:daabdb8037186d1e.title: The Axis of Upheaval Goes to War
d006da4fe3:daabdb8037186d1e.author: Andrea Kendall-Taylor, Richard Fontaine
d006da4fe3:daabdb8037186d1e.summary: Andrea Kendall-Taylor and Richard Fontaine, former members of the National Security Council, argue that the members of what they call the “axis of upheaval”—Russia, China, Iran, and North Korea—are deepening their cooperation. Meanwhile, Washington is creating friction with many of its own partnerships. If these developments continue unabated, the United States will squander the strength of its network just as its adversaries learn to make the most of theirs.

d006da4fe3:960aafc689650ffc.title: The Nuclear Deal That Could Save NATO
d006da4fe3:960aafc689650ffc.author: Ivo H. Daalder
d006da4fe3:960aafc689650ffc.summary: Former U.S. NATO ambassador Ivo Daalder argues that the scramble to shore up Europe's conventional defense risks overlooking the continent's greatest security weakness: nuclear deterrence. Europe knows it can't fully trust Washington's guarantee anymore. But he lays out a middle path between dependence and nuclearization that would extend France's and the United Kingdom's nuclear umbrella—a course, he argues, that could even repair the transatlantic alliance.

fc066e842d:33b974b735b72e1c.title: Intangible Capital as a Source of Economic Growth and Productivity: A Literature Review and Policy Guidelines
fc066e842d:33b974b735b72e1c.author: Rouvinen, Petri
fc066e842d:33b974b735b72e1c.summary: Abstract This review synthesizes the latest scholarly evidence on intangible capital. Drawing on 60 recent studies across macro, meso, and micro levels (anchored by firm-level data from Finland, broader Europe, the US, and Asia) it demonstrates that intangible investments have emerged as the preeminent engine of economic growth, competitiveness, and productivity. The literature yields three critical imperatives for public policy. First, the measurement and statistical tracking of intangibles require a fundamental overhaul; at present, a swath of these investments remains invisible in official data and absent from corporate balance sheets. Second, policymakers must broaden their horizons beyond narrow research and development (R&D) subsidies. Modern innovation policy must embrace the full spectrum of intangible assets – spanning software, data, organizational capital, management capabilities, and brand equity –, while capitalizing on the vital synergies between them. Third, the scalable nature of intangible capital demands a synchronized approach to competition policy, innovation strategy, and corporate finance. Authorities must strike a delicate balance: cultivating the incentives and finance necessary to fuel intangible investments, while simultaneously preventing harmful market concentration and fostering broad diffusion of knowledge.

fc066e842d:ab0dcab8e5d42453.title: Economists, Economic Knowledge, and Central Banks
fc066e842d:ab0dcab8e5d42453.author: Juan Acosta
fc066e842d:ab0dcab8e5d42453.summary: What do economists do in central banks? Why do central banks hire economists? This book investigates the evolving role of economists and economic knowledge within central banks, arguing that their current centrality is neither self-evident nor historically inevitable. While the presence and influence of economists in central banks today may seem natural, this book shows that it is the result of a complex, gradual, and uneven historical process shaped by institutional structures, disciplinary transformations, and shifting relationships between science and policy. Drawing on a rich but dispersed body of literature, the book traces how economists progressively gained authority through the establishment of statistics departments, the adoption of macroeconometric models, and the emergence of a shared cognitive infrastructure between academia and central banks. Rather than focusing on individuals or doctrines, it examines general trends and institutional shifts across a series of national case studies to show how central banks function as boundary organizations, at the intersection of policy and science.

fc066e842d:61d4ea428c9550d8.title: Known Unknowns: Knowledge, Confidence, and Public Opinion on Water Reuse
fc066e842d:61d4ea428c9550d8.author: Marco Dâ€™Errico
fc066e842d:61d4ea428c9550d8.summary: Public acceptance can constrain treated-wastewater reuse, but less is known about whether citizens provide a substantive view at all. An influential account of opposition to contested technologies predicts that the strongest opponents know the least while believing they know the most. We test that joint prediction using a knowledgeâ€“attitudesâ€“practices survey of 1, 069 households in Barbados. The survey separately measures demonstrated topic knowledge, self-assessed knowledge, willingness to use reclaimed water, and explicit 'donâ€™t know' responses. Among respondents who provide a complete willingness profile, demonstrated knowledge is essentially unrelated to acceptance, whereas self-assessed knowledge is positively associated with acceptance. The predicted knowledge-overconfidence configuration therefore does not appear in this setting. The strongest knowledge gradient instead lies on the response margin: a one-standard-deviation increase in demonstrated knowledge is associated with a 5.8-percentage-point lower probability of giving at least one 'donâ€™t know' response, against a base rate of 22.6 per cent. The relationship reappears in three sectoral attitude batteries and attenuates by about 19 per cent after controlling for out-of-module nonresponse. The evidence therefore points away from confidently mistaken opposition and toward a sizeable group that is less knowledgeable and more likely to express uncertainty.

fc066e842d:d765895f74b481b4.title: Venture Capital and Customer Capital
fc066e842d:d765895f74b481b4.author: Amir Sufi
fc066e842d:d765895f74b481b4.summary: Venture capital specializes in the financing of customer capital intensive firms—firms with higher sales and marketing expense to revenue ratios, a higher wage bill for sales and marketing employees, and a higher tendency to apply for trademarks—and they do so more than other financial intermediaries. Venture capitalists target high customer capital industries with low knowledge capital but avoid high knowledge capital industries that lack customer capital. Firms tilt investment toward customer capital leading up to the initial venture capital investment, after which their scale accelerates rapidly. Venture capitalists focus on financing customer capital because such investments require tolerance for substantial risks of failure in pursuit of extreme upside potential, as characterized by power law returns. This return profile fits customer capital investments more closely than investments in knowledge capital. Venture capitalists that sprinkle small investments across a large number of firms, colloquially referred to as the “spray and pray” strategy, target customer capital industries for investment, whereas venture capitalists that commit larger amounts to a small number of firms target knowledge capital industries. The venture capital focus on customer capital reflects a shift away from its traditional focus on knowledge capital intensive firms over the past 30 years.

fc066e842d:d77e3040274eaa10.title: From Balanced Growth to Innovation Cycles: A Solow-Type Semi-Endogenous Growth Model
fc066e842d:d77e3040274eaa10.author: Thi Kim Cuong Pham
fc066e842d:d77e3040274eaa10.summary: We develop a growth model with an R&D sector in which the elasticity of innovation with respect to existing knowledge can be negative. We investigate the existence and uniqueness of a balanced growth path (BGP) and derive closed-form growth factors, showing that productivity and output growth are semi-endogenous and population-driven. We also establish the global stability under a general production function. Under testable parameter restrictions, the economy converges to the BGP. However, when the knowledge elasticity is sufficiently low, a Jacobian-based condition implies instability, and an N-period innovation cycle can emerge. Comparative statics are conducted to explore the impact of several factors, including research efficiency, input elasticity, and population growth. Numerical simulations map out transitions and mark the points at which stability is lost. They make clear when innovation frictions endanger balanced growth and provide practical guidance for R&D and demographic policy.

5b51167fb0:0132a15a91a18b86.title: The Returns to Government R&D: Evidence from US Appropriations Shocks
5b51167fb0:0132a15a91a18b86.author: info@aeaweb.org (Andrew J. Fieldhouse1 and Karel Mertens2 1 Mays Business School, Texas A&M University (email: afieldhouse@mays.tamu.edu) 2 Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, CEPR (email:…
5b51167fb0:0132a15a91a18b86.summary: American Economic Review 116 (11): 3959-4002 Abstract Based on a narrative classification of all significant postwar changes in R&D appropriations for five major federal agencies, we find that an increase in nondefense R&D appropriations leads to increases in various measures of innovative activity and higher business-sector productivity in the long run. We structurally estimate the production function elasticity of nondefense government R&D capital using the SP-IV methodology of Lewis and Mertens (2024) and obtain implied returns of 140 to 210 percent over the postwar period. The estimates indicate that government-funded R&D accounts for one-fifth of business-sector TFP growth since WWII and imply substantial underfunding of nondefense R&D. (JEL D24, E23, H50, O31, O33, O38)

5b51167fb0:c7fa8e0ff8b591f9.title: The Unequal Economic Consequences of Carbon Pricing
5b51167fb0:c7fa8e0ff8b591f9.author: info@aeaweb.org (Diego R. Känzig1 1 Northwestern University, CEPR, and NBER (email: dkaenzig@northwestern.edu))
5b51167fb0:c7fa8e0ff8b591f9.summary: American Economic Review 116 (11): 4003-4040 Abstract This paper studies the economic impacts of carbon pricing. Exploiting institutional features of the European carbon market and high-frequency data, I identify carbon policy shocks and trace their dynamic effects. A restrictive carbon policy shock raises energy prices, reduces emissions, spurs green innovation, but decreases economic activity—disproportionately burdening poorer households. Not only are the poor more affected because of their higher energy spending, but they also experience larger income losses. These indirect, general equilibrium effects via income and employment play an important role in the transmission of carbon pricing policies, accounting for about two-thirds of the aggregate consumption response. (JEL E23, E24, O44, Q41, Q54, Q55, Q58)

5b51167fb0:e824f86123436e63.title: Residential Segregation and Unequal Access to Local Public Services in India: Evidence from 1.5 Million Neighborhoods
5b51167fb0:e824f86123436e63.author: info@aeaweb.org (Sam Asher1, Kritarth Jha2, Paul Novosad2, Anjali Adukia2 and Brandon Tan3 1 Imperial College London (email: sam.asher@imperial.ac.uk) 2 Development Data Lab (email:…
5b51167fb0:e824f86123436e63.summary: American Economic Review 116 (11): 4041-4076 Abstract We study residential segregation and access to public services across 1.5 million urban and rural neighborhoods in India. Muslim and Scheduled Caste segregation in India is high by global standards and only slightly lower than Black-White segregation in the United States. Within cities, public facilities and infrastructure are systematically less available in Muslim and Scheduled Caste neighborhoods. Nearly all regressive allocation is across neighborhoods within cities—at the most informal and least studied form of government. These inequalities are not visible in the aggregate data typically used for research and policy. (JEL H76, J15, O15, O17, O18, R23)

5b51167fb0:ed6f6ae7997930cd.title: Durables and the Marginal Propensity to Spend
5b51167fb0:ed6f6ae7997930cd.author: info@aeaweb.org (Nathan Zorzi1 and Martin Beraja2 1 Dartmouth (email: Nathan.G.Zorzi@dartmouth.edu) 2 UC Berkeley and NBER (email: maberaja@berkeley.edu))
5b51167fb0:ed6f6ae7997930cd.summary: American Economic Review 116 (11): 4077-4115 Abstract Durables represent a large share of households' marginal propensity to spend (MPX). We develop a quantitative model of spending that takes durables into account and matches a rich set of empirical regularities simultaneously. Scaling the response of nondurables provides a poor approximation of the MPX on durables when it comes to its distribution in the population, its persistence over time, and its cyclicality. As an application, we study how the MPX varies with the size of stimulus checks and find that it declines more slowly compared to a model of purely nondurable spending. (JEL D11, E21, E32, E62, G51)

5b51167fb0:3196e21e18145698.title: Union Bargaining Power and the Amenity-Wage Trade-Off
5b51167fb0:3196e21e18145698.author: info@aeaweb.org (Lorenzo Lagos1 1 Brown University, NBER, and IZA (email: lorenzo_lagos@brown.edu))
5b51167fb0:3196e21e18145698.summary: American Economic Review 116 (11): 4116-4157 Abstract This paper studies how collective bargaining affects wages and amenities. By merging collective bargaining agreements (CBAs) to linked employer-employee data in Brazil, I combine rich contracted amenities with wage information. I implement a difference-in-differences strategy that exploits a court ruling enforcing CBA continuation (i.e., ultra-activity) to estimate the effects of union bargaining power. Strengthening unions raises wages and amenities without reducing employment—increasing retention despite some labor-labor substitution. A revealed-preference approach shows that amenities account for 45 percent of total compensation gains. These findings suggest that collective bargaining can offset monopsony power, but employers retain the right-to-manage workforce composition. (JEL J31, J32, J42, J51, J52, O15)

5b51167fb0:040a01a62b7769bc.title: Inequality and Racial Backlash: Evidence from the Reconstruction Era and the Freedmen's Bureau
5b51167fb0:040a01a62b7769bc.author: info@aeaweb.org (Eric Chyn1, Kareem Haggag2 and Bryan A. Stuart3 1 Department of Economics, University of Texas-Austin, and NBER (email: eric.chyn@austin.utexas.edu) 2 Anderson School of Management,…
5b51167fb0:040a01a62b7769bc.summary: American Economic Review 116 (11): 4158-4202 Abstract How do majority groups respond to narrowing inequality in racially polarized environments? We study this by examining the Freedmen's Bureau, an agency created after the US Civil War to aid former slaves and launch institutional reform in the South. Using new historical records and an event-study approach, we estimate the bureau's impact on political, social, and economic outcomes. Vote shares for Democrats, the party that previously championed slavery and opposed Black civil rights, initially eroded in bureau counties, but these impacts faded as federal oversight weakened. Racial backlash emerged rapidly and persisted, suggesting White majorities sought to offset Black progress. (JEL D63, D72, J15, N31, N41)

5b51167fb0:0ad09d14a2108386.title: The Inflation Attention Threshold and Inflation Surges
5b51167fb0:0ad09d14a2108386.author: info@aeaweb.org (Oliver Pfäuti1 1 The University of Texas at Austin (email: pfaeuti.oliver@gmail.com))
5b51167fb0:0ad09d14a2108386.summary: American Economic Review 116 (11): 4203-4242 Abstract The recent inflation surge brought inflation back on people's minds. I quantify when and how much attention to inflation changes and derive the macroeconomic implications of these attention changes. I estimate an attention threshold at an inflation rate of 4 percent, that attention doubles when inflation exceeds this threshold, and that supply shocks have stronger and more persistent effects on inflation in times of high attention. Developing a model featuring the attention threshold, I show that attention changes offer a joint explanation for inflation surges, inflation's co-movement with inflation expectations, and a long last mile of disinflation. (JEL D84, E12, E31, E43, E52)

5b51167fb0:cde519eb240cea67.title: The Causal Effects of Global Supply Chain Disruptions on Macroeconomic Outcomes: Evidence and Theory
5b51167fb0:cde519eb240cea67.author: info@aeaweb.org (Xiwen Bai1, Jesús Fernández-Villaverde2, Yiliang Li3 and Francesco Zanetti4 1 Tsinghua University (email: xiwenbai@mail.tsinghua.edu.cn) 2 University of Pennsylvania (email:…
5b51167fb0:cde519eb240cea67.summary: American Economic Review 116 (11): 4243-4281 Abstract We study the causal effects of global supply chain disruptions by constructing a new index of real-time port congestion using Automatic Identification System data from container ships and a spatial clustering algorithm. We develop a model with search frictions between producers and retailers that links upstream production slack to downstream supply shortages and captures output and price responses to supply chain shocks. The co-movements of output, prices, spare capacity, and market tightness provide novel identification restrictions. We find that demand and supply shocks drove US disinflation in 2020, while the inflation surge in 2021 was driven mainly by supply chain shocks. (JEL C43, E31, F14, F23, L14, L92)

5b51167fb0:e1d96c9b68fa4eb6.title: Firm Adaptation in Production Networks: Evidence from Extreme Weather Events in Pakistan
5b51167fb0:e1d96c9b68fa4eb6.author: info@aeaweb.org (Clare Balboni1, Johannes Boehm2 and Mazhar Waseem 1 London School of Economics and Political Science (email: c.a.balboni@lse.ac.uk) 2 University of Geneva (email:…
5b51167fb0:e1d96c9b68fa4eb6.summary: American Economic Review 116 (11): 4282-4325 Abstract This paper considers how far private adaptation may reduce future vulnerability to climate risks. Using data on monthly firm-to-firm transactions from Pakistan, we find that flood-affected firms are more likely to relocate to safer ground and shift purchases toward suppliers in less flood-prone regions and reached via less flood-prone roads. The results indicate that firms are imperfectly informed about flood risk and update their beliefs following floods. We quantify aggregate impacts using a spatial model of endogenous production network formation. The findings suggest that firms' learning will shape the economic impact of increasingly frequent climate-related disasters. (JEL D22, L14, O13, O14, Q54, R32)

5b51167fb0:f3cbadd0645f288a.title: Reproducible Aggregation of Sample-Split Statistics
5b51167fb0:f3cbadd0645f288a.author: info@aeaweb.org (David M. Ritzwoller1 and Joseph P. Romano2 1 Stanford University (email: ritzwoll@stanford.edu) 2 Stanford University (email: romano@stanford.edu))
5b51167fb0:f3cbadd0645f288a.summary: American Economic Review 116 (11): 4326-4357 Abstract Statistical inference is often simplified by sample splitting. This simplification comes at the cost of the introduction of randomness not native to the data. We propose a simple procedure for sequentially aggregating statistics constructed with multiple splits of the same sample. The user specifies a bound and a nominal error rate. If the procedure is implemented twice on the same data, the nominal error rate approximates the chance that the results differ by more than the bound. We illustrate the application of the procedure to several widely applied econometric methods. (JEL C20, C30, C52)
